newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Telesystem of Canada launches Romania's first GSM.
newsitem.headline: Telesystem of Canada launches Romania's first GSM.

text.p: A consortium led by Canada's Telesystem International Wireless (TIWC) launched on Tuesday Romania's first GSM cellular telephone system with hopes to attract over one million subscribers in a $500 million project.

"We launched the system by providing GSM coverage to Bucharest and eight major cities," Al Tolstoy, President of Connex GSM -- a brand name chosen by the Mobifon consortium to run the project -- told Reuters during the launching ceremony.

Tolstoy said he was confident Connex GSM would be successful in the Balkan country as the wireless market in Romania holds strong potential for development. Some 3.1 million of its 23 million people subscribe to the fixed network, a penetration rate of only 13 percent, one of the lowest in Europe.
He said Connex was planning a fast roll-out of the project and cover with the new digital system Romania's main cities and European transit routes within the next 12 months.
"We count on over one million subscribers. Roaming is going to be put in place this summer after we complete the necessary agreements with other countries," Tolstoy said.
Ex-communist Romania is the last state in the region to set up a digital GSM system.

Last November, Mobifon won one of the two licences offered in a tender by the Communications Ministry. The other winner was the Mobilrom consortium, led by France Telecom. Mobilrom is expected to become operational in a few months.

Tolstoy said Connex had encountered several obstacles during the first stage of the project, including a temporary plunge of the local leu currency earlier this year "which made some of our partners very nervous."
In February, the leu fell to some 9,000 to the dollar from 4,050 last December. It is now around 7,000 to the dollar.
Leapfrogging generations of technology and connecting Connex's GSM network cells to the land lines of Romania's Romtelecom phone operator added to the problems, he said.
"But now everything is up and running perfectly," he said,
The licence has a 10-year validity and frequency concession tax amounted to $50 million. Connex would spend $500 million on the project and create over 500 new jobs, he said.

Apart from TIWC, Mobifon includes AirTouch Communications Inc. of the United States and Romanian partners Posta Romana post authority, the private Ana Electronics retailer, Logic Telecom data network operator, ISAF engineering firm and the Romanian Investment Fund.
